title: Uninformed Search: BFS, DFS, UCS
overview: Study search strategies that use only the problem definition, without any estimate of distance to the goal.
objectives: Explain uniform-cost search for weighted graphs
Compare memory use and optimality of each strategy

method.title: Breadth-first
method.body: Uses a FIFO queue and expands the shallowest node first; it finds the fewest-step solution but may use lots of memory.

method.title: Depth-first
method.body: Uses a stack and goes deep first; it needs little memory but is not complete on infinite or cyclic spaces without checks.

method.title: Uniform-cost
method.body: Expands the node with the lowest path cost using a priority queue, giving optimal solutions for nonnegative costs.

method.title: Iterative deepening
method.body: Repeats depth-limited DFS with increasing limits to combine low memory with BFS-like completeness.

pseudocode:
BFS: frontier = queue([start])
DFS: frontier = stack([start])
UCS: frontier = priority_queue(key=path_cost)
while frontier:
    n = frontier.pop()
    if goal(n): return n
